Two different mechanisms decide what happens to people after a state, and a model needs the right one. In a **split on entry**, the outcome is decided when people enter the state: here, 10% of infectious people will go to hospital and the rest will recover, each after their infectious period. With **competing hazards**, two transitions out of a state run at the same time and whichever happens first wins: here, people in hospital are discharged after 10 days on average, but die at a rate of 0.02 per day while they are there, so the share who die depends on both rates. This page puts both in one model, a respiratory infection with hospitalization, and checks the share who die. Then it makes the chance of hospitalization depend on age, written as a Python function, and runs the model both as compartments and as agents.

## The model

| Parameter | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| β | 0.3 per day | Rate of infection |
| Infectious period | 8 days | Mean time in I (exponential), before recovery or hospitalization |
| Hospitalized | 10% | Share of infectious people who go to hospital, decided on entry to I |
| Stay in hospital | 10 days | Mean time to discharge |
| Death in hospital | 0.02 per day | Rate of death while in hospital, competing with discharge |
| R0 | 2.4 | β × the infectious period |
| Population | 100,000 | |
| Infectious at the start | 0.1% | |

The model is written as a function of the chance of hospitalization, so that the same model can be made again with a chance that depends on age, [below](#severity-by-age-as-a-function):

```{python}
import starsim as ss

def make_covid(hospitalized=0.1):
    """ An SIR with hospitalization and death; hospitalized is the chance of going to hospital """
    S, I, R, H, D = ss.states('S I R H D')
    infection = S >> I @ 0.3*I
    course    = ss.Transition(I, {R: None, H: hospitalized}, dur=ss.days(8))  # Split on entry: 10% to H, the rest to R
    discharge = H >> R @ ss.days(10)                                            # Competing hazards: discharge ...
    death     = H >> D @ ss.perday(0.02)                                        # ... and death
    return ss.Disease(infection, course, discharge, death, init=dict(I=0.001), name='covid')

covid = make_covid()
```

In `{R: None, H: 0.1}`, `None` stands for the rest (here, 90%). The diagram, from `diagram()`:

```{python}
covid.diagram()
```

And the equations, in which the split appears as the shares (1 - 0.1) and 0.1 of the flow out of I, and the competing hazards as two flows out of H:

```{python}
covid.equations()
```

A rate given as a number is named by its transition, so the rate of death appears as a parameter called `rate_death`, and a duration by the state it is the time in (`dur_I` and `dur_H`). To give it a name of your own, write it as `ss.par(ss.perday(0.02), name='mu')` (see [Parameters](../user_guide/building_parameters.qmd)).

## Result

```{python}
sim = ss.Sim(covid, total_pop=100_000, stop=ss.days(200))
sim.run()
sim.plot('covid')
```

Of the people admitted to hospital, the share who die is the rate of death over the sum of the two rates out of H: 0.02 / (0.02 + 1/10) = 1/6. The flow `course.H` is the number admitted to hospital:

```{python}
admitted = sim.results.covid['course.H'].sum()
deaths = sim.results.covid.death.sum()
print('Admitted:', round(admitted), 'Died:', round(deaths), 'Share:', round(deaths/admitted, 3))
```

## Severity by age, as a function

Some parts of a model are easiest to write as a function. Here the chance that an infection is severe enough for hospital depends on age: 10% under 50, and 40% from 50 up. Rather than stratify the disease by age and give a value for each group, the chance is a Python function of the sim, which reads people's ages. Starsim tries the function on the model's age groups, and since it works on them, the model still runs as compartments; run as agents, the same function is evaluated for each person.

```{python}
def severity(sim):
    """ The chance of hospitalization: 10%, plus 30% from age 50 """
    return 0.1 + 0.3*(sim.people.age >= 50)

covid_age = make_covid(hospitalized=severity)
```

The sim is split into two age groups at 50 (`stratify=dict(age=[0, 50])`), so that the function has ages to work on in a compartmental run. The same model is run as an ODE and as agents, in a population of 10,000:

```{python}
sims = {
    'ODE': ss.Sim(covid_age, total_pop=10_000, stop=ss.days(200), stratify=dict(age=[0, 50]), verbose=0),
    'Agents': ss.Sim(covid_age, total_pop=10_000, stop=ss.days(200), solver='abm', verbose=0),
}
msim = ss.parallel(sims)
msim.plot('covid')
```

The two agree, apart from chance in the agent run. Of about 8,800 infections, about 1,500 people are admitted to hospital (`covid_course.H`): about one in six, between the 10% of those under 50 and the 40% of those over, since about a quarter of people are 50 or over (the population's ages are guessed as the world's in 2024, as `describe()` says). Of those admitted, one in six die, as before, since the competing hazards out of H haven't changed:

```{python}
msim.summarize().loc[['covid_infection', 'covid_course.H', 'covid_death']]
```

A function that needs each person (one that takes `uids`, the people it applies to, as well as the sim) can't be run as compartments, so Starsim runs a model with one as agents, and `describe()` says why.
